setlist_extra.title: Next Time You See Me Jam

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jam** (4 reviews): The jam right after Drums is a wild Jerry showcase, said never to recur in the next 28 years; The opening jam features open, free exploration with Jerry and Phil pushing hard together [4][5][11][12]
- **It's A Sin** (1 review): Reviewer finds the opening Jam into It's A Sin breathtaking [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Lovelight Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]
- **'It's In The Book'**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Eleven Jam**: rare: 10 archived performances [15]
- **The Seven**: rare: 4 archived performances [15]
- **break with chatter**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Next Time Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Rub Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Look On Yonder Wall**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Other One Jam [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-10-10.sbd.hollister-konstantin-hoelter.5186.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 164 min; rated 2.83/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Set 1 mix sits hard in the left or right channel, with almost nothing centered; set 2 mix differs [1]
- **gd68-10-10.sbd.miller-ladner.4513.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 167 min; rated 4.14/5 by 35 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer expected sparse music without Bob and Pig, but the reduced lineup works very well; Reviewer finds the sound remarkably good for 1968; Reviewer says the sound is surprisingly good for 1968, pairing it with the 10/30/68 show [5][6][8][11]

## Around the show

- Reviewer sees the show as a catalyst for the more jazz-based sound of the early 1970s [3]
- Reviewer calls it some of the loosest free-form jamming ever, comparing it to Miles Davis [6]
- Reviewer considers the music well beyond what the full Dead were doing at this point [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-10-10.sbd.hollister-konstantin-hoelter.5186.shnf**: transferred by See info file; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Source is a DAT to ZA2 to wav chain, cut in Sound Forge; the uploader brought it from Arizona on a hard drive [1]
- **gd68-10-10.sbd.miller-ladner.4513.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller and neo_levo; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Lineage is soundboard to reel to CD, possibly with an extra reel generation; seeds came from c.miller; Transfer was done in DAE and shnv3 by neolevo [2]
